To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the method of rearing, caging density and LLV infection had significant effects on performance of laying hens, and that the commercial stock and the crosses were superior to the control strains.

(1) the method of brood-rearing had a small but significant effect on the adult performance of chickens; (2) there were large differences in adult performance between control strains and the commercial stock; (3) the method of housing in the laying house had significant effects on the performance of hens; and (4) LLV infection was detrimental to egg production.
the method of rearing and housing had no significant effect on the frequency with which birds shed LLV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
genetic and environmental factors that affect adult performance of egg-type chickens.
genetic, environmental, and infectious disease factors that influence the performance of laying hens.
the effects of genetic and environmental factors on egg production and egg size, and with the relationship between LLV infection and egg production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of brood-rearing and rearing had only small effects on performance and that the method of housing had only minor effects on mortality and egg production.

the method of brood-rearing and rearing affected some performance traits but not others, that there were differences in adult performance of birds reared at the two sites, that there were genotype-site and genotype-method of housing interactions, that the frequency of shedder was not affected by brood-rearing or housing method but that LLV infection was a serious problem.
the genetic background of a stock is the primary determinant of adult performance, but that geographical area, reared method, caging densities, and LLV infection can have important secondary effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are significant effects of genetic strain and geographical area on performance and LLV infection, but that the effects of caging density and method of brooding are small and of little practical importance.
the effects of LLV on adult performance are more important than the effects of rearing method and caging density.

the method of brood-rearing had no effect, that the method of laying house-testing had some effect, that the geographical area had some effect, and that the genotype had the largest effect on the traits measured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method of brooder rearing and the method of caging density in the laying house have a major effect on adult performance of egg-type chickens.
the effects of genotype, site, method of brooding, method of rearing, and caging density were large, but the effects of LLV infection on performance were even larger.
the method of brood-rearing, caging density and LLV infection can have a significant impact on adult performance in chickens.
